messages:
Maya Patel: FYI reproducible hang in Go quickstart generator sample when cancelling ctx during streaming. Repro: start stream, cancel parent ctx after ~200ms, goroutine count increases and process doesn't exit cleanly.

Maya Patel: Snippet:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 150*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, model, opts)
for stream.Next() {
  fmt.Println(stream.Token())
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { log.Println("stream error:", err) }
```

Chris Nguyen: Two suspects: transport not using req.WithContext or an auth refresher goroutine ignoring ctx.

Maya Patel: Sample helper does start a tiny token refresher that auto-retries on 401.

Sasha Ivanov: If retry/backoff uses time.Sleep without select on ctx.Done() we'll leak goroutines.

Priyanka Rao: Also ensure Generator.Stream wires ctx into the http.Request so the underlying read unblocks — otherwise Next() can hang.

Chris Nguyen: Grep shows http.NewRequest(...) then a go doRetry(req) spawning attempts that write to a channel without honoring ctx.

Alex Gomez: Reproduced with pprof; goroutines stuck in time.Sleep inside retry loop. Gist: https://gist.github.com/xxx/quickstart-stream-ctx-leak

Priyanka Rao: Fix plan: 1) use req = req.WithContext(ctx) 2) make retry/backoff ctx-aware (select over time.After and ctx.Done) 3) expose Stream.Close()/Cancel() in SDK and demo it in quickstart.

Sasha Ivanov: Docs/UX note: examples should prefer ctx-aware sleep helpers and show explicit Close so newcomers don't rely only on parent ctx.

Alex Gomez: I'll open a small PR: respect ctx in retry, use WithContext on transport, add sample Close demo and README note. ETA EOD tomorrow.

devex-bot: CI queued (quickstart-tests) job #4921

Maya Patel: Assign follow-ups in GH issue #789. Thanks all.
